title: Commercial Natural Gas Supply: Correct Swing Excess Amount and Over-Billing on a Swing Excess Line
content:
A swing excess correction on a Commercial Natural Gas Supply agreement is worked on the agreement's most recently posted swing excess charge line, taken with the energy charge line of the same billing period start. The over-billed amount on that swing excess line is its billed amount less the correct swing excess amount, never below zero, and it is returned as one rebill credit tied to the line and dated on the correction date.

## What is read from the records

| Item | Source |
|---|---|
| Billed amount, therms, billing period start and end, posted date | The most recently posted swing excess charge line of the agreement |
| Therms billed at the contract price | The energy charge line with the same billing period start |
| Contracted annual therms | The agreement record |
| Delivered index price | The monthly index price notice whose effective date equals the cycle's billing period start |
| Swing tolerance and swing excess adder | The plan's row of the swing bandwidth schedule |

## Quantities

1. **Cycle usage** — the therms on that cycle's energy charge line plus the therms on the swing excess line.
2. **Monthly contract volume** — the contracted annual therms divided by 12 and rounded half up to a whole therm.
3. **Upper end of the band** — the monthly contract volume multiplied by (100 plus the swing tolerance) percent, rounded half up to a whole therm, where the swing tolerance is the plan's swing tolerance percentage.
4. **Measured excess therms** — the cycle usage less the upper end of the band, never below zero. The correct excess therms are the measured excess therms.
5. **Price per correct excess therm** — the delivered index price of the cycle's notice plus an adder equal to the plan's swing excess adder.
6. **Correct swing excess amount** — the correct excess therms multiplied by that price per therm, rounded half up to the cent.
7. **Over-billed amount** — the billed amount of the swing excess line less the correct swing excess amount, never below zero.
8. **Rebill credit** — the over-billed amount plus any overcharge interest due, rounded half up to the cent; it is posted as a negative amount.

## Worked example (hypothetical agreement on the Fixed 12 plan: swing tolerance 20 percent, swing excess adder $0.0400 per therm)

Contracted annual therms 15,000. The most recent swing excess line bills 260 therms for $171.60; the energy charge line of the same cycle bills 1,500 therms; the cycle's index notice shows $0.5800 per therm.

- Monthly contract volume: 15,000 divided by 12 is 1,250 therms.
- Upper end of the band: 1,250 multiplied by 120 percent is 1,500 therms.
- Cycle usage: 1,500 plus 260 is 1,760 therms; measured excess 260 therms, which are the correct excess therms.
- Price per therm: $0.5800 plus $0.0400 is $0.6200; correct swing excess amount 260 multiplied by $0.6200 is $161.20.
- Over-billed amount: $171.60 less $161.20 is $10.40. With no overcharge interest due, the rebill credit is $10.40, posted as minus $10.40.

## Edge cases (hypothetical)

| Situation | Over-billed amount |
|---|---|
| Cycle usage does not exceed the upper end of the band, yet a swing excess line was billed for $95.00 | Measured excess is 0, correct amount $0.00, over-billed $95.00 |
| Billed amount $150.00 and correct swing excess amount $162.00 | Never below zero, so $0.00 |
